result.summary: This pull request is an explicit test-only branch that modifies socket sending logic to artificially fragment all outbound networking data into small chunks. It serves as a reproducer to identify test framework and node code that makes invalid assumptions about TCP packet chunking, and includes fixes for several functional tests handling partial reads in HTTP and P2P handshakes.
result.problem: Functional tests and networking components sometimes assume that a single socket read will return a full message, header, or HTTP response. On slow or congested networks, TCP segmentation breaks data across multiple reads, causing tests such as interface_http.py and P2P v2 tests to fail or time out intermittently.
evidence: PR description: 'This branch contains a stress test reproducer. For every socket send, sending is changed to break up data in small chunks... The goal is to test code for robustness in face of unexpected chunking of the data.'

Commit 9f7ae464aa explains: 'Several checks read a response with one recv() call (recv_raw(), up to 1024 bytes) and assumed it held the whole HTTP response. TCP does not guarantee this: on a slow or loaded machine a response can arrive split across several reads...'
Referenced spin-off PRs and issues: #36726, #36729, and #36730 extract the genuine fixes identified by this test run.
result.scope_notes: This PR is marked draft and DONTMERGE by the author; it mixes diagnostic instrumentation into the node's network layer with actual test fixes meant to be cherry-picked into standalone pull requests.
result.card: This test-only PR forces all node socket sends to be fragmented into small chunks to stress-test Bitcoin Core and its test suite against arbitrary TCP segmentation. It exposes latent flakiness in functional tests that incorrectly assume incoming HTTP responses or P2P handshakes arrive in a single read. The branch is explicitly not intended for merge, acting as an incubator and reproducer for standalone bugfix PRs like #36729 and #36730.

risk.why: This is a marked DONTMERGE test run, but if merged accidentally the artificial send fragmentation would cause severe network degradation and CI failures.
